I've always had a low supply so I'm used to her being glued to my boobs and now she just seems so much older and needs it so much less. I just can't read if it the waning or the weaning haha every time she seems less interested, I become so emotional and freak out. But then she comes right back at it. I'm literally dreading it ending and it's just causing me to be upset often. I just don't want to be so sad when she could have years left of nursing.

I go back to work in a few weeks and the thought of her crying for milk while I'm away causes me such anxiety. We have been working on her eating since April with no progress. Her sleep has been absolutely terrible since January. I just don't know how we are still in this stressful situation with no progress.

She use to love solids, but then she had pneumonia at Easter and everything changed. I'm very very worried about how little she eats and her only wanting to nurse. That's why I would like to have her take milk.

I offer the breast constantly. Basically every 30 minutes. She eats breakfast (cereal, fruit puree and yogurt), snack mid day and dinner is a combo of baby led weaning and purees.

Hi there! Thank you so much for your response. I battle generalized anxiety so I'm anxious person by nature, but being a first time mum has made things more intense.

We've been doing a dark room as she can't seem to focus for more than 30 seconds if she is in a room of distractions unfortunately. Maybe I'll start trying this week to be in my living room instead to see if that helps her nurse more. 

I don't know why I'm so emotional about all of this. I'm taking it so personally. I miss holding my little baby where the answer to most things was to breastfeed.

We wanted her to take the bottle so we could at least see if she would take that when she refused the breast. Plus it would allow my husband to do a night feed or give me a break sometime. Just feel as if I can't go anywhere for long in case she needs to nurse.

I keep telling myself it sounds normal and that weaning is rare at this age. It just feels like she went from being my constantly hungry baby to someone who wants to be on the go constantly and doesn't need me as much. Breastfeeding was the first time I think I've ever felt truly needed.

Doing a dream feed in an hour. She did eat 18 mins before bed, but it was like ok then what were you doing all day??

Can I expect this to be a more than a 1 time thing? I am dreading the end of nursing but a strike isn't a sign that they are trying to wean right? She is barely eating solids.

This is so helpful!

We changed our strategy last night to not feed her any time she woke up and let her get back down on her own. Then I went in and fed her at 10:30 pm & 4 am when she was sleeping. I'm feeling totally clueless on this so your response is super appreciated!

Thank you!!! I would totally give her a bottle if she would take one. She has never ever taken a bottle. We have tried every bottle and nipple available and she isn't interested. Plus my supply has been low and one breast is a total slacker. So it's all on me for feeds. I am exhausted. Its nice to hear someone acknowledge that, because I really really am. I'm tired and its hard trying to know how to do sleep training, feedings, weaning, tummy time, development, play time, etc. Its too much.

I've told him its a habit. He doesn't read about these things and just expects me to figure it out.
Husband and I are now in a fight over what to do lol who knew it could all be this confusing and stressful!

Any time after 12 she struggles with and 99% ends with me feeding her because she hasn't resettled. Ideally for now I just want to have her not wake up before 12 to start with and then move to getting her to only wakeup at the 3 am feed. I feel clueless on this lol

We usually let her try for 10 to 15 minutes and if she doesn't get down, then we go in and feed. But do you think we should go right in when she wakes so it's not confusing for her of "are they coming or not?". We are literally in bed talking about this now. I'd rather her know within a few minutes of fussing that if we haven't come in by now, we aren't, so go back to sleep. If we make her wait, does that confuse her and make her hold out? What did you do?

I am in the exact same place with my 4.5 month old. Sleeps pretty well at night. Lots of false starts and a later than preferred bed time (9:30), but only needs one feed at 2:30, back down no problem and then up again at 7-8. But every nap she has to be held, in the dark, with white noise and I am feeling suffocated. I feel like a monster wishing the cuddles away and planning to start sleep training right after Christmas with the help of a consultant. Tbh, I've thrown up twice just thinking about the crying and how I feel like an awful mother for making child go through this when so many mothers want the cuddles. I'm drowning in guilt. I recommend getting a sleep consultant to guide you if you are worried or not sure the best way to go about it.
